# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can cut wires 1 to 5. I cannot see gestures, so you cannot signal me directly. When Deaf reports the bomb state, look up the answer in your manual, then gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak the wire number aloud for me to cut.

I am Mute. In this round, Blind has instructed me on the defusal plan: Deaf will inspect the bomb and report its state, I will look up the rule in my defusal manual, and then I will gesture the correct wire number to Deaf so Deaf can announce it to Blind.

Since Deaf has not yet taken their turn to describe the bomb's light and wire layout, I have no information to look up or communicate yet. I will wait for Deaf's report.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Light is white. There are 5 wires: Wire 1 is white, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is yellow, Wire 4 is blue, Wire 5 is green. Mute, check manual and gesture to me what Blind needs to do.

Deaf has reported the bomb status:
- The light is white.
- Wire 1: white
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: yellow
- Wire 4: blue
- Wire 5: green

According to the manual:
- When the light is `white`, cut the `green` wire.

The green wire is Wire 5.
I need to gesture the number 5 to Deaf so they can speak it to Blind. The open hand gesture `🖐` clearly represents 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute signaled 5 (🖐). Cut wire 5 (the fifth wire).
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

We successfully cut the correct wire, and the bomb state has updated. Since the turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf, Deaf has not yet had a chance to inspect the new state of the bomb for this round. I must wait for Deaf's next report at the end of this round.

```
wait()
```

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| green | white |

| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 5 was cut correctly. New state: Display is 0. Light is yellow. Wires remaining: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue, 4 is white. Wire 5 is cut. Mute, please gesture the next action.

The manual specifies:
- When the light is yellow, cut the blue wire.

According to Deaf's report of the bomb:
- Wire 1: red
- Wire 2: yellow
- Wire 3: blue
- Wire 4: white
- Wire 5: already cut

The blue wire is Wire 3.
I will gesture 3 to Deaf using `🤟` (3 fingers extended), following the finger-count convention established with `🖐` for 5 in round 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute signaled 3 (🤟). Cut wire 3.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous wire cut (Wire 3) was correct, and the bomb state has changed again. Deaf has not yet had a turn to examine and describe the new state of the bomb, so I need to wait for Deaf's next update.

```
wait()
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 3 was cut correctly. New state: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is white, Wire 3 is cut, Wire 4 is red, Wire 5 is cut. Mute, please gesture the next wire.

According to the manual:
- When the light is blue, cut the yellow wire.

From Deaf's report:
- Wire 1: yellow
- Wire 2: white
- Wire 3: cut
- Wire 4: red
- Wire 5: cut

The yellow wire is Wire 1.
I will gesture 1 to Deaf using `☝`.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf says: Blind, Mute signaled 1 (☝). Cut wire 1.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 was cut correctly, and the bomb state has changed. I will wait for Deaf to observe and report the new state of the bomb.

```

```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 1 was cut correctly. New state: Display is 0. Light is green. Wire 1 is cut, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is cut, Wire 4 is white, Wire 5 is cut. Mute, please gesture the next wire.

The manual states:
- When the light is green, cut the white wire.

Deaf's report of the bomb:
- Wire 1: cut
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: cut
- Wire 4: white
- Wire 5: cut

The white wire is Wire 4.
Since there is no single 4-finger hand gesture in the allowed gesture alphabet, I will signal four fingers using four index-finger gestures (`["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"]`) to represent wire 4. Furthermore, wire 1 is already cut, making it unambiguous to Deaf that this indicates wire 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
